*New.* Hong Kong Free Press and the South China Morning Post reported Demosisto's dissolution on June 30, 2020. Studentlocalism and the Hong Kong National Front ended their Hong Kong operations the same day.

*New.* The Associated Press and CNN reported the Hong Kong Police Force statements of July 1, 2020. The first arrest came shortly after midday. Police reported about 370 arrests that day, ten under the new law.

*New.* Implementation Rules for Article 43, gazetted July 6, 2020. The rules cover content removal and data demands, interception on executive authorization and penalties for service providers who refuse. The Office for Safeguarding National Security opened on July 8, 2020. The police national security department dates from June 30, 2020.

Apple Daily printed its final edition on June 24, 2021. Stand News closed on December 29, 2021, after a police raid and arrests. Citizen News announced its closure on January 2, 2022. Prosecutors charged the forty-seven on February 28, 2021, as the British government's six-monthly report for that half year records. Public libraries began withdrawing books for review in July 2020.

Britain and the People's Republic signed the Joint Declaration on December 19, 1984, and registered it with the United Nations. The National People's Congress adopted the Basic Law in April 1990, and it took effect on July 1, 1997.

Decision of the National People's Congress of May 28, 2020, on the legal system and enforcement mechanisms for safeguarding national security in Hong Kong. Decision of the National People's Congress of March 11, 2021, on improving the city's electoral system. The Standing Committee then amended Annexes I and II of the Basic Law. **Corrected.** The first edition attributed the March 2021 decision to the Standing Committee alone.

The Security Bureau froze HK$18 million of assets held by three Apple Daily companies on June 17, 2021. The sum equals about US$2.3 million. Company filings and Security Bureau statements carry the figure. **Verified.**

Police arrested Jimmy Lai and searched Apple Daily on August 10, 2020. Police put the number of officers at about two hundred. Apple Daily streamed the search live on its Facebook page, as Global News and Nieman Lab reported.
